title: Majestic Win: The Final King Escape
summary: Choose the precise king route out of rook checks; the opponent’s own pawn limits how long the rook can keep checking.

nodes.question: Which king escape preserves the win?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Rxa4+. White’s a-pawn has just been removed, leaving a seven-piece position. White must answer the rook check against Kg4.

branches.title: Advance past the rook’s checking range
commentary: Begin after ...Rxa4+. White’s a-pawn has just been removed, leaving a seven-piece position. White must answer the rook check against Kg4.
Kg5 is the only legal move that preserves a forced win in this exact diagram. It advances toward the h7 pawn rather than retreating.
Ra5+ follows the king upward with another rook check. This is the selected source reply.

Kh6 escapes to the sixth rank. The black a6 pawn prevents another check by moving the rook from a5 to a6. The exact remaining position is winning for White; other rook or knight defenses and the later conversion are outside this short selected line.

exercises.prompt: How does Black’s extra pawn interfere with its rook?
exercises.answer: Once the rook checks from a5 and White reaches h6, a6 is occupied by Black’s own pawn. The rook cannot continue the same checking ladder onto a6.

startContext: Begin after ...Rxa4+ at 169 seconds, the visually reconstructed seven-piece diagram with Kg4. The earlier nine-piece rook checks, sacrifice on g1 and eight-piece knight-underpromotion phase remain source context. This study verifies the final unique king move, the illustrated ...Ra5+ Kh6 continuation, and two independently tested drawing errors; it stops before claiming a complete conversion.
